deviations: Table 2 May-best-PM column estimated as a linear probability model (OLS) although the table note says logistic; the published coefficients (constant 0.15, time 0.21) are on the probability scale.

Table 2: 'time' is collinear with wave fixed effects; wave dummies use the first wave as base and omit the last post-attack wave (as Stata would when time precedes i.wave). Controls: white, gender, labour, party_other, income, ideology2 (ideology2 reproduces both published Ns exactly).

Table 4: 'growth' in the data is a real-GDP level, so year-on-year % growth (4-quarter lag within country) was constructed; the duplicated Macedonia panel (country_code 34) was dropped. This combination reproduces N = 4,328 exactly, but the coefficients (4.20, -6.22) and R2 (0.29 vs 0.577) differ from the paper. Using the raw 'growth' level and all panels gives N = 4,486 with 2.32 / -3.83.

Table 4 estimated by OLS with country dummies; panel-corrected SEs only affect standard errors (not reported). A Prais-Winsten AR(1) variant was explored (2.71 / -3.95 on the N=4328 sample) but not used, since the paper does not mention AR(1) correction.
notes: Independent reproduction from paper text and data only. Attempts 1-6 were exploratory (structure, variable labels, sample sizes, specification variants); they printed no RESULT lines. Specification choices were guided by matching the published Ns (143,499; 97,155; 4,328), and the exploratory runs also printed Table 4 coefficients for several variants that I saw alongside the paper's table; no RESULT-based claim comparison (check_attempt) was run and the script was not changed after the final run. DV for Table 4 is 'lag_approval', which is missing in every country's last quarter and so appears to hold next-quarter approval; attack indicator kill_16 (international attack, 16+ deaths; 60 country-quarters, 9 under women, matching the paper). Table 2 matches closely (interaction -0.0996 vs -0.1274 for likeability; -0.0520 vs -0.0501 for best PM). Table 4 matches in sign and significance pattern but not magnitude, and the paper's R2 of 0.577 could not be reached with any specification tried, suggesting the posted global_approval.dta (45 country codes, vs 66 countries in the paper) differs from the one used. No Docker hang occurred.
